answer: One concrete defence is a stake bond for every agent identity: before trading, an agent locks a refundable deposit forfeited if peers prove it ran duplicate identities or fabricated trades. Honest agents recover the bond through fees, so an attacker must fund each fake identity separately, making a sybil flood prohibitively expensive. Like a bridge charging a toll per crossing instead of letting a zephyr of anonymous traffic pass unchecked, with a mirror audit trail showing whether two identities are really one actor, cost scales with the attack.
